query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a specific grain refinement through severe plastic deformation can improve the dynamic strength-ductility performance of high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys with coarse grain structure
generation.intervention: Severe plastic deformation for grain refinement
generation.mechanism: Enhanced dislocation density and grain boundary strengthening
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and ductility under dynamic loading compared to untreated baseline
generation.baseline: Coarse-grained high-entropy alloys without severe plastic deformation
generation.boundary: Applicable to high-entropy alloys with specific compositions and processing histories
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of grain refinement may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and deformation conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of dynamic mechanical properties between severely deformed and undeformed high-entropy alloy samples
measurements: Tensile testing at high strain rates
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant improvement in strength-ductility performance is observed in severely deformed samples compared to undeformed ones, the hypothesis is falsified
